results.title: Fake news in Africa: In an age of disinformation, who decides what's true?
results.content: From Ghana to Mozambique, the fight against fake news keeps gaining momentum. But combating disinformation also requires safeguards for free speech, leaving some governments in an inconvenient position.

results.title: Strait of Hormuz still a source of leverage for Iran
results.content: Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz put crews at risk and drive up energy shipping costs. Iran's ability to sustain them and the limits of US protection will shape how much trade can continue and at what price.

results.title: EU aims to pick new ECB chief by year-end
results.content: Christine Lagarde's decision to step down early as head of the European Central Bank (ECB) has put the European Union on a tight schedule. The bloc expects to pick a new ECB chief by the end of December.

results.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
results.content: The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

results.title: South Africa elections: ANC marks its worst-ever performance
results.content: The African National Congress, the party of late liberation icon Nelson Mandela, slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. Voters blame the ANC for water and electricity shortages.

results.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
results.content: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

results.title: Israeli president tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
results.content: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government. Tricky coalition talks are expected.

results.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
results.content: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

results.title: Should AI companies pay for the journalism they use?
results.content: Publishers say AI chatbots are using their reporting to answer readers' questions while sending back less traffic and less money. Should the companies that build these tools pay for the journalism they rely on?

results.title: Son of Iran's shah receives 'Freedom Prize' in Frankfurt
results.content: 18,000 people gathered in Frankfurt to show support for Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Iranian monarch ousted in 1979. Factions in the opposition have accused him of not distancing himself from his father's rule.

results.title: After victory in the midterms, what next for US Democrats?
results.content: Donald Trump's Republican party has lost its majority in both chambers of the US Congress. But the president still has a lot of power — and the Democrats have yet to agree on how best to use theirs.

results.title: New Zealand election too close to call with over 95% of votes counted
results.content: Initial results in New Zealand show the two main parties neck-and-neck with fewer than 4,000 votes separating them. Official results aren't expected until later this month once special votes have been counted.
